xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5218: CodeRabbit findings relayed just before merge are lost: file a follow-up issue after merge (never gating)

plan.title: CodeRabbit findings relayed just before merge are lost: file a follow-up issue after merge (never gating)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: One vertical feature: the relay records what a follow-up needs, a pure per-thread settlement rule decides, a filer creates the issue, a post-merge kick and a deacon-lite patrol trigger it. Splitting into sibling issues would ship a journal shape nothing reads, or a filer nothing triggers durably.

narratives.Problem: A CodeRabbit finding relayed to a work agent is lost when the PR merges before the agent acts on it (PAN-5198 / PR #5203: delivered at 21:00:37, merged at 21:10:53, nothing in between). The feedback body asks the agent to open a follow-up if the PR already merged, but nothing makes sure that happens. CodeRabbit must stay advisory and never gate a merge.
narratives.Proposal: The CodeRabbit relay journals repo, PR number, review id/url and the thread list on feedback.delivered, and journals feedback.undelivered on every Needs-you branch. A pure settlement function decides per thread: a non-CodeRabbit reply on the thread, a later single-parent PR commit that changed the thread's file, or a later review.requested note naming the thread id settles it; a failed read counts as no evidence. fileAdvisoryFollowups files one App-authored GitHub issue per delivery with unsettled threads (after a body search for the delivery key), journaling feedback.followup_filed, or raises Needs-you and journals feedback.followup_failed. Two non-gating triggers: a fire-and-forget kick in postMergeLifecycle after merge.completed, and a deacon-lite patrol that re-runs the filer for merged issues with pending candidates (merge.completed >= 10 min old, candidate >= 2 min old), covering restarts and relays that finish after the merge.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Changing the Flywheel author/assignee gate (roles/flywheel.md, sync-sources/skills/pan-flywheel/SKILL.md, tests/unit/prompts/prompt-invariants.test.ts) to accept overdeck-agent
- Granting the GitHub App issues: write, or editing scripts/create-github-app.mjs
- Filing follow-ups as the gh user, or on Linear, GitLab, Jira or Rally trackers
- Backfilling deliveries journaled before this change (entries without data.threads are skipped)
- Automatic retry after a recorded feedback.followup_failed
- Strict exactly-once issue creation across processes (one issue per key on every normal path is the guarantee)
- Any merge gate, merge delay, or merge-readiness read of CodeRabbit state; merge-agent.ts must not mention coderabbit
- Changing how last-entry journal readers (deacon-lite.ts recoverStalledReviews, undispatched-review-recovery.ts, pr-outside-pipeline.ts) treat feedback entries
- Editing src/dashboard/server/main.ts or raising any file-size allowlist row

autoDecisions.summary: File follow-ups only through the GitHub App; on any failure (including the missing issues: write permission) raise Needs-you instead of falling back to the gh user.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue specifies a bot-authored issue and names Needs-you as the failure path; filing under the operator's identity from server code is a policy change nobody asked for.

autoDecisions.summary: A reply on a CodeRabbit thread from anyone other than coderabbitai[bot] is the agent's explicit skip for that thread.
autoDecisions.rationale: The relay body already tells the agent to reply with its reason when it rejects a finding and says it is then done; inventing a second skip channel would leave replied findings to be filed as noise.

autoDecisions.summary: Settlement is per thread and tied to the thread (reply on it, later commit changing its file, re-review note naming its id); a failed forge read counts as no evidence, so the thread is filed.
autoDecisions.rationale: A PR-wide commit or a generic CodeRabbit note would settle unrelated findings (plan critique round 1); a redundant follow-up costs one closed issue, a false 'settled' loses the finding.

autoDecisions.summary: Do not change the Flywheel author gate in this issue; report the panopticon-agent[bot] vs overdeck-agent mismatch to the orchestrator.
autoDecisions.rationale: The gate is a security rail pinned by prompt-invariants.test.ts, and follow-up bodies quote third-party CodeRabbit text, so auto-trusting them is a separate security decision.

autoDecisions.summary: Name the new entry feedback.followup_filed exactly as the issue does; name the no-agent entry feedback.undelivered.
autoDecisions.rationale: Reviewers verify against the issue text; the issue names the entry explicitly.

autoDecisions.summary: Two triggers: a non-awaited kick in postMergeLifecycle after merge.completed, and a deacon-lite patrol that re-runs the filer for merged issues with pending candidates.
autoDecisions.rationale: The relay is not awaited and can journal after merge.completed, and nothing re-runs a finished lifecycle; the journal candidate is the durable job record, and main.ts has no file-size headroom for a new dashboard service.

autoDecisions.summary: Non-GitHub trackers (resolveGitHubIssue returns isGitHub false) raise Needs-you with the findings instead of filing.
autoDecisions.rationale: The bot identity and the Flywheel gate are GitHub concepts; creating Linear/GitLab issues is out of scope.

autoDecisions.summary: Dedup is the journal marker plus a GitHub search for the delivery key in issue bodies before creating; strict exactly-once across processes is not promised.
autoDecisions.rationale: appendPipelineEntry never reports a failed write; the search repairs the marker on a retry, and a cross-process lock is out of proportion for an advisory feature.

autoDecisions.summary: List every unsettled thread in the follow-up body with no cap; a body GitHub rejects is a filing failure with the full list in Needs-you.
autoDecisions.rationale: A cap would drop findings, which is the bug being fixed.
